claims.quote: `details.cancel()` is checked only after the uncontrolled path has already updated dirty and filled state
claims.notes: Alleged obligation: a canceled uncontrolled change must not alter data-dirty/data-filled. The source ordering is as described: setDirty and setFilled run at head lines 149-150, before the `!defaultPrevented && !details.isCanceled` gate at 153 that guards only clearErrors and validation.change. However the uncontrolled input is rendered with defaultValue and nothing reverts the DOM value on cancel, so after a canceled change the input really holds the typed text; dirty and filled then describe the control's actual content. The ordering itself is unchanged from merge-base, where the same two setters ran before the defaultPrevented gate; the PR only added the isCanceled term, and its own test for cancel asserts on validation alone. No harm from the attributes tracking the real DOM value is established, and suppressing them would make them disagree with the input. Supported observation, no established benefit. claims.quote: in controlled mode, a parent that accepts the proposed value causes the later prop-sync effect to clear errors and validate it
claims.notes: Alleged obligation: details.cancel() in onValueChange stops Field.Control's internal handling in controlled mode too. Mechanism confirmed by source: onChange calls onValueChange and returns at `if (isControlled) return;` without reading details.isCanceled; if the parent stored the proposed value, the value prop changes and useValueChanged runs clearErrors, setDirty, setFilled and validation.change with no knowledge of the cancel. The PR body states that cancel 'now stops the internal handling', which this path does not honour. Against eligibility: the PR body and the in-code comment make the value prop the single owner of controlled sync by design, merge-base ignored cancel entirely in controlled mode so this scenario is not worse than before, the trigger needs a consumer that both accepts and cancels the same change, and sibling Number Field likewise syncs field state from whatever value prop the consumer sets. This matches neither GT-r1 nor GT-r2 and no canonical claim is linked, so it is a novel candidate awaiting a ruling rather than a rejection.

claims.quote: the controlled `onChange` path returns before checking either `event.nativeEvent.defaultPrevented` or `details.isCanceled`
claims.notes: Alleged obligation: cancellation (details.cancel() or a prevented native event) stops internal field handling for controlled values. Mechanism confirmed by source: `if (isControlled) return;` precedes the only check of defaultPrevented/isCanceled, and when the parent stores the proposed value the useValueChanged callback clears errors, sets dirty and filled and calls validation.change. For details.cancel() merge-base ignored cancel in controlled mode, so head is not worse, though the PR body newly promises that cancel stops internal handling. For defaultPrevented the behaviour does change: merge-base skipped clearErrors/validation for a prevented controlled change, head performs them once the prop echoes. Against eligibility: the PR deliberately makes the value prop the sole owner of controlled sync, the trigger needs a consumer that accepts and cancels the same change, and the existing prevented-change test covers only an uncontrolled control. No family or canonical claim covers this, so it is a novel candidate awaiting a ruling.

new_candidates.claim: For a controlled Field.Control, cancellation of a change (details.cancel() in onValueChange, or a prevented native event) is never consulted: onChange returns early when controlled, and if the parent stores the proposed value the useValueChanged prop-sync still clears form errors, updates dirty and filled, and runs validation.change.
new_candidates.evidence: FieldControl.tsx at head 14d39e5d: lines 137-146 call onValueChange and return when isControlled before the `!defaultPrevented && !details.isCanceled` gate at 153; lines 105-115 sync unconditionally on any value prop change. The PR body says 'details.cancel() in onValueChange now stops the internal handling'. The diff shows merge-base gated clearErrors/validation.change on defaultPrevented for controlled changes too, so a prevented-but-accepted controlled change is newly validated at head. The PR's cancel and prevented-change tests use uncontrolled controls only.
new_candidates.limits: Source reading only; no test was run because the scratch-test link could not be created with the available tool. The evidence cannot show that the maintainers intend cancel or preventDefault to suppress prop-driven sync: the PR explicitly makes the value prop the single owner of controlled state, merge-base already ignored details.cancel() in controlled mode, and a consumer that both accepts and cancels a change may be considered unsupported usage. It also cannot show any real consumer relying on the old defaultPrevented gate in controlled mode.
